subject: Alternate sourcing: bundle vs consumption — decision grid and ask
messages:
From: Tom Raines <tom.raines@cloudpilot.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 05 Jun 2028 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Initial replacement proposition for CloudPilot (pricing + onboarding)

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. As promised, attached is a concise replacement proposal that addresses CloudPilot's core asks: price parity on inference unit cost, a staged onboarding credit to offset migration effort, and an option for a short-term seat-based overlay while they verify runtime compatibility. High-level: a 12-month committed consumption discount (20% off published), $50k migration credit applied as prepaid usage, and a 60-day pilot with production-like SLA for latency.

Two quick clarifications we need from you to make this binding:
- Your preferred metric for parity: per-token runtime (p50) or per-inference-unit (50ms bucket)?
- Any minimum throughput burst requirements (we saw notes about occasional 50k token spikes per minute).

If you want I can reformat into a decision grid (cost vs ops risk vs legal exposure) for your procurement team.

Attaching: cloudpilot_offer_v3.pdf (proposal), pricing-assumptions.xlsx (raw assumptions).

Best,
Tom
Tom Raines
Director, Strategic Accounts — CloudPilot
T: +1 415-555-0198

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Raines <tom.raines@cloudpilot.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 05 Jun 2028 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial replacement proposition for CloudPilot (pricing + onboarding)

Tom —

Thanks, I reviewed the PDF quickly. Can you hold off on DocuSign until we have one internal pass? We'll need a short decision artifact that lays out the trade-offs (I asked procurement for "cost per equivalent inference unit", but for ops our SREs prefer a latency/SLA overlay).

I asked Marissa to jump in here to do a commercial comparison and produce a simple decision grid we can share with CloudPilot procurement — columns: annual $TCO, migration friction (low/med/high), SLA risk (low/med/high), rollback exposure, and contract complexity (one vs two agreements). Can you confirm the following so we can fill the grid?
- Exact quoted unit (is discount on 'inference-unit-hour' or 'token' pricing?).
- Whether the $50k migration credit requires prepayment or is billed as a credit after go-live.
- Any clipping on burst allowance in month 1.

Also attaching a template we use for these comparisons (redwood_decision_template.xlsx). If you can return the completed grid by end of day Thursday, we can move fast.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
+1 650-555-0123

From: Tom Raines <tom.raines@cloudpilot.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudpilot.com
Date: Wed, 06 Jun 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial replacement proposition for CloudPilot (pricing + onboarding)

Irene —

Appreciate the template, attached is cloudpilot_offer_v3.pdf (updated) and price_comparison_sheet.csv with the line-by-line unit mapping. Quick answers inline:
- Discount applies to our "inference-unit-hour" (IUH) SKU; for tokenized models we map tokens -> IUH using the sequence-length assumptions in the CSV.
- $50k migration credit can be structured either as prepaid usage (applied to invoice) or as a post-go-live credit; default we do invoice credit to speed sign.
- Burst: first 30 days include a 2x burst allowance above committed throughput; sustained overages bill at the overage rate.

We've also added a DocuSign link (https://docusign.com/AA1234567) for the commercial term sheet if you want to circulate — but happy to wait while you do an internal grid.

Let me know if you want me to pre-populate your template; I can do that today.

Best,
Tom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 06 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: CloudPilot offer — draft grid and recommendation

Irene / Jonas — forwarding Tom's update after I pre-filled the decision template with our estimates. Attached: price_comparison_sheet.csv (from them) + my completed redwood_decision_template.xlsx (summary pasted below).

-- Pasted decision grid (summary) --
Options considered:
1) Full migration — commit 12m consumption (20% discount) + $50k migration credit
   - Annual $TCO (est): $1.1M
   - Migration friction: Medium (data egress + test harness work)
   - SLA risk (latency): Low-medium (we can hit p95 targets with config)
   - Rollback exposure: Medium (customer state and KV cache size)
   - Contract complexity: Single agreement (preferred)

2) Hybrid overlay — seat-based overlay for first 90 days + consumption commit
   - Annual $TCO (est): $1.25M (higher short term)
   - Migration friction: Low (maintain legacy for short period)
   - SLA risk: Low (fallback to legacy)
   - Rollback exposure: Low
   - Contract complexity: Two agreements (adds ops handshake)

3) Short pilot then re-bid — 60-day pilot, no commit
   - Annual $TCO (est): Unknown (higher variability)
   - Migration friction: Low-medium
   - SLA risk: Medium-high (no committed capacity)
   - Rollback exposure: Low
   - Contract complexity: Minimal (pilot terms)

Recommendation: pursue Option 2 (Hybrid overlay) as the lowest operational risk while securing a 12-month commitment that preserves most of the TCO benefit. Key ask from CloudPilot: make migration credit payable on invoice and guarantee a 2x burst for first 30d. If they accept that structure I recommend we sign commercial term sheet and run a 90d overlay pilot with telemetry gating.

Action items:
- Irene: confirm to Tom that we want migration credit as invoice-applied and ask procurement to include rollback credit (if performance delta > 20% at p95 we push for $25k credit).
- Jonas: please draft the SRE acceptance criteria for the pilot (p50/p95 latency, error budget).
- Marissa: will draft the commercial note for procurement to review.

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Raines <tom.raines@cloudpilot.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, procurement@cloudpilot.com
Date: Thu, 07 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial replacement proposition for CloudPilot (pricing + onboarding) — confirmation and next steps

Tom —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for confirming the burst and credit structure. After an internal pass we want to move forward with a Hybrid overlay (Option 2) under these conditions:
- Migration credit: $50k applied as invoice credit on first billing cycle (no prepayment).
- Pilot & overlay: 90d seat-based overlay + consumption commit (12m) to activate the 20% discount after pilot completion.
- Burst: 2x burst allowance for first 30 days.
- Rollback protection: if p95 latency delta >20% vs baseline during the first 60 days after cutover, CloudPilot will provide a $25k rollback credit applied to the next invoice.

Please review and confirm acceptance of those bullets so we can route to legal and procurement for signatures. We'll also need telemetry hooks (basic tracing spans + tokenized request sampling) to validate p95 during pilot — Jonas, please coordinate SRE acceptance criteria with Tom once he confirms.

If you can update the DocuSign with these bullets in an addendum I'll route immediately. Looking to have signed commercial terms by end of next week.

Cheers,
Irene
